q: Global asymptotic stability of ẋ = f(x) can be established by finding a Lyapunov function V: ℝⁿ → ℝ that is positive definite, radially unbounded (V(x) → ∞ as |x| → ∞), and satisfies V̇ < 0 for x ≠ 0. Radial unboundedness ensures:
opts: All sublevel sets {V ≤ c} are compact, so trajectories cannot escape to infinity
exp: Radially unbounded (V → ∞) Lyapunov functions ensure that all level sets are compact, so trajectories are bounded for all time. Combined with V̇ < 0, this gives global (not just local) asymptotic stability.
